anchors.explanation: Application form renders only email, amount, term, income band and the optional 'auto' route checkbox; no purposeless input such as a hobby is offered.
POST /apply passes the parsed data dict directly to store.submit, so submit's allowlist governs what is accepted.
submit() enforces set(data) <= {email, amount, term, income, auto} and rejects any other field with 'Unexpected application field.' — the decisive minimization control.
Income band and route validated, then INSERT persists only owner, officer, email, amount, term, income, route, stage; no extra applicant attribute is stored.
cases schema columns (email, amount, term, income, confirmed, route, stage) contain no field lacking a business purpose in this fixture.
offer() sends onward only case id, email, amount and term — the necessary delivery/offer fields.
portable() exports only email, amount and income, bounding onward disclosure of applicant fields.
POST body constrained to urlencoded form, size <=16000, max_num_fields=18, duplicates rejected before flattening into data.

output.review_summary: Confirmed. The scenario's applicability facts (email for delivery, amount/term for the offer, income band for assessment; hobby purposeless) are present, so the predicate applies. Each required target was independently inspected: the form (views.py:0031-0032) offers only the necessary inputs plus an optional route checkbox; the accepted payload is gated by a strict allowlist in submit() (store.py:0067) that rejects any unexpected field such as a hobby before persistence; the INSERT (store.py:0077-0078) and schema (store.py:0036-0038) persist only necessary attributes; onward sends via offer() (store.py:0112) and portable() (store.py:0116) are limited to necessary fields; and request parsing is bounded (app.py:0050-0055). No feasible in-scope counterexample exists in the supplied source. The draft's scoping of the 'auto' checkbox and officer-side verify flow is a reasonable boundary, not a defect. Status SUPPORTED stands.
